newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna toasts Fergie before Opera Ball.
newsitem.headline: Vienna toasts Fergie before Opera Ball.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York arrived in Vienna on Thursday for the prestigious Opera Ball and was promptly whisked off by her Prince Charming for the evening, tycoon Richard Lugner, for a spot of book signing.

Sarah Ferguson appeared in a bottle-green suit with fur lapels flanked by two men dressed in ceremonial Guards uniform in Lugner City, a modern shopping mall, to sign copies of her autobiography "My Story".

"I haven't had such an amazing welcome for a long time," the duchess popularly known as "Fergie" told a crowd of some 2,000 flag-waving Austrians lining the three floors of the neon-lit shopping centre.
Fergie, whose 10-year marriage to Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew ended in divorce last year, said she did not know if she would dance at Vienna's most historic ball.
"I don't know if I will have time. I will have to practise my waltz this afternoon," she said to loud cheers and applause.
Although the setting was not exactly regal and lacked a traditional red carpet, Fergie's host laid on a brass band to welcome his princess with the British national anthem.
Lugner, 64, who made his fortune in the construction industry and is ridiculed in Austrian society as a flashy parvenu, could hardly conceal his excitement to have British blue blood by his side.
"You can't go any higher than that," he exclaimed. "I can't believe she's really here," he added.
The magnate is reported to have paid 461,000 schillings ($40,000) for the privilege of having the flame-haired duchess on his arm.
That does not include the three-room suite at the lavish Imperial Hotel, where Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler stayed, or two stretch limousines to ferry Fergie around.

Lugner, nicknamed "Moertel", or concrete, because of his profession and his squat appearance, has in the past counted among his guests singer Grace Jones, socialite Ivana Trump and actresses Sophia Loren and Joan Collins.
He openly courts media attention, using glamorous women to promote his marketing strategies. His motto is: "No depths are too low."

Fergie, dubbed "Duchess of Pork" by the British tabloid press in reference to her continual battles with her weight, has recently taken to the public spotlight in an effort to combat her mounting debts.
She struck lucrative deals this month to advertise cranberry juice on television and to be spokeswoman for Weight Watchers International.
